label: In code (Python, JavaScript and similar), the point inside a list literal where its next item is about to start: the line break and indent right after a '[' that opens a multi-line list, or the closing '},' / '),' / '],' of one bracketed item (a dict, object, tuple or inner list) when another item follows inside a list. Inline lists of plain strings or numbers are weak, and C-style '{' arrays weaker; dicts and objects on their own, function-call arguments, append/push calls, '[' used for indexing or type hints, and lists in prose stay quiet.
